name: Container memory pressure
hypothesis: A container may be exceeding its memory limit or the node may be under memory pressure.
mitigation: Consider rolling back the recent release or adjusting memory requests and limits after confirming the cause.

name: Readiness or insufficient healthy replicas
hypothesis: Traffic may be reaching a service with too few ready endpoints.
mitigation: Inspect health probes, release status and capacity before considering a rollback or scaling action.

name: CPU / autoscaling capacity
hypothesis: A scaling limit or resource bottleneck may be contributing to latency or errors.
mitigation: Review HPA limits, pod requests and node capacity; scale only after validating the bottleneck.

name: Container restart loop
hypothesis: The container may be exiting repeatedly due to application, configuration or resource failures.
mitigation: Compare with the last known-good deployment and consider a controlled rollback after approval.

name: Downstream dependency failure
hypothesis: An upstream dependency or network path may be failing; the application itself may still be healthy.
checks: Check service EndpointSlices and DNS resolution
Compare application error logs with dependency latency
mitigation: Verify upstream service health, retry/circuit-breaker behavior and consider traffic shift if a healthy fallback exists.
